question: The cost price of a whiteboard is ₹2,800. The shopkeeper gave 87% of discount on the cost price. What is the selling price (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the discount is 87% directly on the Cost Price, the Selling Price will be the remaining percentage of the Cost Price.

⇒ Selling Price % = 100% − 87% = 13%

⇒ SP = 13% of 2800

⇒ SP = (13 ÷ 100) × 2800

⇒ SP = 13 × 28 = 364

**∴ The correct answer is ₹364.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) of whiteboard = ₹2,800

Discount = 87% on CP

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price − Discount Amount

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount Amount = 87% of 2800

⇒ Discount Amount = (87 ÷ 100) × 2800

⇒ Discount Amount = 87 × 28

⇒ Discount Amount = 2436

⇒ Selling Price = 2800 − 2436

⇒ Selling Price = 364

**∴ The correct answer is ₹364.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Standard Discount Rule

Normally, discounts are given on the Marked Price (MP). So, SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100. However, as explicitly stated in this question, if the discount is calculated on Cost Price (CP), we apply the same logic on CP instead.

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of x% and y% are given back to back, the single equivalent discount % = x + y − (x × y ÷ 100).

Profit and Loss Calculation

Profit % or Loss % is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specified otherwise. Profit = SP − CP, and Loss = CP − SP.
